title: 1 Samuel Chapter 18 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Samuel chapter 18 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 18 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Samuel Chapter 18.

questions.question: What was the relationship between Jonathan and David after Saul finished speaking?
options: Jonathan was jealous of David
Jonathan's soul was knit with David's soul
Jonathan ignored David
Jonathan was afraid of David
questions.correctAnswer: Jonathan's soul was knit with David's soul
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:1 states that Jonathan's soul was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.

questions.question: What did Saul do with David after the conversation ended?
options: Sent him back to his father's house
Made him king immediately
Would not let him go home
Exiled him
questions.correctAnswer: Would not let him go home
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:2 says Saul took David that day and would let him go no more home to his father's house.

questions.question: Why did Jonathan and David make a covenant?
options: Because Jonathan was afraid of David
Because Jonathan loved David as his own soul
Because Saul commanded it
Because David requested it
questions.correctAnswer: Because Jonathan loved David as his own soul
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:3 says Jonathan and David made a covenant because Jonathan loved David as his own soul.

questions.question: What did Jonathan give to David as a sign of their covenant?
options: His crown
His robe, garments, sword, bow, and girdle
A silver necklace
His horse
questions.correctAnswer: His robe, garments, sword, bow, and girdle
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:4 says Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that was upon him and gave it to David along with his garments, sword, bow, and girdle.

questions.question: How did David behave when Saul sent him out?
options: Recklessly and foolishly
Wisely and accepted by all the people
Reluctantly and with fear
He disobeyed Saul
questions.correctAnswer: Wisely and accepted by all the people
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:5 says David behaved wisely and was accepted in the sight of all the people and Saul's servants.

questions.question: What did the women sing when David returned from killing the Philistine?
options: Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands
David is a mighty warrior
Saul is the greatest king
Peace has come to Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:7 records the women's song comparing Saul's thousands slain to David's ten thousands.

questions.question: How did Saul feel about the women's song comparing David to him?
options: He was very pleased
He was indifferent
He was very wroth and displeased
He laughed it off
questions.correctAnswer: He was very wroth and displeased
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:8 says Saul was very wroth and the saying displeased him.

questions.question: What did Saul do from the day he heard the women's song?
options: Promoted David
Eyed David with suspicion
Praised David openly
Ignored David
questions.correctAnswer: Eyed David with suspicion
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:9 states Saul eyed David from that day and forward.

questions.question: What happened to Saul the day after the women's song?
options: He prophesied because an evil spirit from God came upon him
He crowned David king
He fled from the palace
He made peace with David
questions.correctAnswer: He prophesied because an evil spirit from God came upon him
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:10 says the evil spirit from God came upon Saul, and he prophesied in the midst of the house.

questions.question: True or False: Jonathan gave David his sword and bow as a sign of their covenant.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:4 says Jonathan gave David his sword and bow among other garments.

questions.question: True or False: Saul was pleased when David behaved wisely and was accepted by the people.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:8 and 1 Samuel 18:9 show Saul was displeased and eyed David with suspicion despite David’s wise behavior.

questions.question: True or False: David played music to soothe Saul when the evil spirit troubled him.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:10 states David played with his hand as at other times when the evil spirit came upon Saul.

questions.question: True or False: The women’s song said Saul had slain more enemies than David.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:7 says the women sang that Saul had slain his thousands, but David his ten thousands.

questions.question: In 1 Samuel 18, which event happens first?
options: Saul sets David over the men of war
Jonathan and David make a covenant
The women sing about David’s victories
Saul casts a javelin at David
questions.correctAnswer: Jonathan and David make a covenant
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:3 records Jonathan and David making a covenant before David is set over the men of war (verse 5), before the women sing (verse 6), and before Saul casts the javelin (verse 11).

questions.question: What did Saul think David would eventually gain if he kept winning battles?
options: Great wealth
The kingdom
A large army
A royal crown
questions.correctAnswer: The kingdom
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:8 says Saul asked what more David could have but the kingdom, showing his fear of losing it.

medium.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 18 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Samuel Chapter 18 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What was Saul's reaction when the women said David had slain ten thousands and Saul only thousands?
options: He was pleased and honored David
He was very wroth and displeased
He ignored the women’s song
He promoted David immediately
questions.correctAnswer: He was very wroth and displeased
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:8 states that Saul was very wroth and displeased with the saying attributing ten thousands to David and only thousands to himself.

questions.question: Why did Saul fear David according to 1 Samuel 18?
options: Because David was stronger physically
Because David was popular among the people
Because the LORD was with David but had departed from Saul
Because David was secretly plotting against him
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD was with David but had departed from Saul
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:12 explains that Saul was afraid of David because the LORD was with David and had departed from Saul, showing the spiritual basis for his fear.

questions.question: How did David respond when Saul offered his elder daughter Merab in marriage?
options: He accepted immediately
He questioned his worthiness and family status
He refused out of loyalty to Saul's enemies
He demanded a dowry
questions.correctAnswer: He questioned his worthiness and family status
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:18 shows David humbly asking 'Who am I? and what is my life, or my father's family in Israel, that I should be son in law to the king?', indicating his humility.

questions.question: What was Saul's real intention in giving his daughter Michal to David as wife?
options: To strengthen David's loyalty to him
To make David a snare and cause harm to him
To honor David openly before Israel
To secure peace with the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: To make David a snare and cause harm to him
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:21 reveals Saul gave Michal to David intending her to be a snare and that the hand of the Philistines might be against David.

questions.question: What did Saul command his servants to tell David to persuade him to become the king's son-in-law?
options: That the king had delight in him and all servants loved him
That David would inherit the throne immediately
That the dowry would be paid in gold
That the Philistines would be defeated soon
questions.correctAnswer: That the king had delight in him and all servants loved him
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:22 states Saul instructed his servants to secretly tell David that the king delights in him and all his servants love him to encourage marriage.

questions.question: What was David's response to Saul's servants about becoming the king's son-in-law?
options: He said it was an easy thing
He said it was not a light thing because he was poor and lightly esteemed
He demanded a large dowry
He asked for time to consider
questions.correctAnswer: He said it was not a light thing because he was poor and lightly esteemed
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:23 shows David responding that it is not a light thing for him, who is poor and lightly esteemed, to become the king's son-in-law.

questions.question: What dowry did Saul require from David to give him his daughter in marriage?
options: One hundred Philistine swords
One hundred Philistine shields
One hundred Philistine foreskins
One hundred Philistine horses
questions.correctAnswer: One hundred Philistine foreskins
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:25 specifies that Saul demanded an hundred foreskins of the Philistines as dowry for his daughter.

questions.question: What was the outcome after David and his men slew two hundred Philistines?
options: David refused to give the foreskins to Saul
David was given Michal, Saul’s daughter, in marriage
Saul exiled David for boasting
David was made captain over all Israel
questions.correctAnswer: David was given Michal, Saul’s daughter, in marriage
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:27 explains that after David brought the foreskins in full tale, Saul gave him Michal to wife.

questions.question: Based on 1 Samuel 18:11-12, what does the passage teach us about God's presence and human fear?
options: Human fear is unrelated to God’s presence
God’s presence with a person can cause fear in others
Fear only comes from physical threats
God’s spirit always protects kings
questions.correctAnswer: God’s presence with a person can cause fear in others
questions.explanation: Verses 11-12 show Saul's fear of David was because the LORD was with David and departed from Saul, teaching that divine favor can provoke fear in rivals.

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 18:14-15 illustrate the importance of wisdom and God's presence in leadership?
options: Wisdom is less important than strength
God’s presence ensures wise behavior and causes fear in enemies
Leaders are loved only if they are physically strong
Fear of leadership always comes from jealousy
questions.correctAnswer: God’s presence ensures wise behavior and causes fear in enemies
questions.explanation: Verses 14-15 show David behaved wisely in all ways and the LORD was with him, causing Saul to fear him, illustrating the link between wisdom, God's presence, and leadership respect.

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 18:16 teach about community response to faithful leadership?
options: Leaders should avoid public attention
All Israel and Judah loved David because of his faithful leadership
Popularity is unrelated to behavior
Only Saul’s servants loved David
questions.correctAnswer: All Israel and Judah loved David because of his faithful leadership
questions.explanation: Verse 16 states that all Israel and Judah loved David because he went out and came in before them, showing that faithful leadership earns communal love.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Samuel 18:19, Merab was given to David as Saul's daughter in marriage.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:19 says that Merab was given to Adriel the Meholathite, not David, showing Saul did not give her to David as promised.

questions.question: True or False: Michal, Saul’s daughter, loved David and this pleased Saul.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:20 records that Michal loved David, and when this was told to Saul, it pleased him.

questions.question: True or False: Saul removed David from his presence because he was jealous of David's popularity among the people.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:13 explains Saul removed David because he feared him due to the LORD being with David and departing from Saul, not specifically due to popularity.

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 18:17-18 show the contrast between Saul’s intentions and David’s humility?
options: Saul wanted David to be valiant in battle, David questioned his worthiness
Both Saul and David eagerly anticipated the marriage
Saul ignored David, David refused the offer
Saul and David plotted together against the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: Saul wanted David to be valiant in battle, David questioned his worthiness
questions.explanation: In verse 17, Saul offers his daughter Merab if David fights the LORD's battles, but David humbly questions his own life and family status in verse 18, showing his humility.

hard.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 18 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Samuel Chapter 18.

questions.question: What was Saul's true intention in giving Michal to David as a wife?
options: To honor David as his son-in-law
To make David a snare and have the Philistines defeat him
To unite the kingdom through marriage
To reward David for his victories
questions.correctAnswer: To make David a snare and have the Philistines defeat him
questions.explanation: Saul said he would give Michal to David so she might be a snare to him and that the Philistines' hand might be against him, intending harm rather than honor (1 Samuel 18:21).

questions.question: How did Saul communicate his plan to David about becoming his son-in-law?
options: He spoke directly to David
He sent a public proclamation
He commanded his servants to speak secretly to David
He sent a messenger to David's father
questions.correctAnswer: He commanded his servants to speak secretly to David
questions.explanation: Saul commanded his servants to secretly commune with David and tell him the king delighted in him and desired him as son-in-law (1 Samuel 18:22).

questions.question: What was David’s initial reaction to the proposal of becoming the king’s son-in-law?
options: He eagerly accepted
He questioned his worthiness due to his low status
He demanded a large dowry
He refused outright
questions.correctAnswer: He questioned his worthiness due to his low status
questions.explanation: David responded by asking who he was, a poor and lightly esteemed man, that he should become the king’s son-in-law (1 Samuel 18:23).

questions.question: What dowry did Saul require from David before giving him his daughter Michal in marriage?
options: One hundred pieces of silver
One hundred Philistine foreskins
A thousand sheep
The capture of a Philistine city
questions.correctAnswer: One hundred Philistine foreskins
questions.explanation: Saul required a dowry of one hundred Philistine foreskins, hoping David would be killed in the attempt (1 Samuel 18:25).

questions.question: How did David respond to Saul’s dowry challenge?
options: He declined the challenge
He accepted and succeeded in killing two hundred Philistines
He asked for more time
He asked for help from Saul’s army
questions.correctAnswer: He accepted and succeeded in killing two hundred Philistines
questions.explanation: David and his men killed two hundred Philistines, doubling the required number, and brought the foreskins to Saul (1 Samuel 18:27).

questions.question: What was Saul’s reaction after David brought the Philistine foreskins and received Michal as a wife?
options: He was pleased and promoted David
He acknowledged the LORD was with David and became more afraid
He immediately reconciled with David
He celebrated with the people
questions.correctAnswer: He acknowledged the LORD was with David and became more afraid
questions.explanation: Saul recognized the LORD was with David and that Michal loved him; consequently, Saul became even more afraid and his enemy continually (1 Samuel 18:28-29).

questions.question: What does the phrase 'David behaved himself more wisely than all the servants of Saul' in verse 30 imply about David’s status and favor?
options: David was less wise and disliked
David had surpassed Saul's servants in wisdom and esteem
David was only favored by Saul’s enemies
David was a poor leader but brave
questions.correctAnswer: David had surpassed Saul's servants in wisdom and esteem
questions.explanation: This verse shows David’s superior wisdom and increasing esteem among the people compared to Saul's other servants (1 Samuel 18:30).

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is thematically connected with David’s covenant of friendship with Jonathan in this chapter, illustrating faithful friendship?
options: Genesis 2:18
Exodus 20:12
Psalm 23
questions.explanation: Ruth 1:16-17 expresses a deep covenant of loyalty and love similar to Jonathan’s covenant with David, reflecting faithful friendship and commitment (1 Samuel 18:3).

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated 'covenant' in 1 Samuel 18:3 (בְּרִית, berith) primarily signifies what kind of relationship?
options: A casual agreement
A solemn, binding agreement between parties
A business contract
A familial tie by blood
questions.correctAnswer: A solemn, binding agreement between parties
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'berith' means a solemn and binding covenant, reflecting the serious commitment Jonathan and David made (1 Samuel 18:3).

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of David's anointing and God’s favor departing from Saul found in this chapter?
options: Acts 13:22
Matthew 5:9
Romans 8:28
John 1:1
questions.correctAnswer: Acts 13:22
questions.explanation: Acts 13:22 recounts David as a man after God’s own heart and the LORD’s favor departing from Saul, connecting with the theme in 1 Samuel 18:12.

questions.question: What literary device is exemplified by the contrast between Saul's increasing fear and David’s rising favor in this chapter?
options: Chiasm
Irony
Parallelism
Foreshadowing
questions.correctAnswer: Irony
questions.explanation: The irony lies in Saul’s fear increasing as David’s favor and wisdom grow, despite Saul being king; this reversal highlights Saul's decline and David’s ascent (1 Samuel 18:28-29, 30).

questions.question: True or False: Saul's initial plan was to strengthen David's position by marrying him to his daughter Michal.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Saul’s plan was to entrap David by giving him Michal, hoping the Philistines would kill him, not to strengthen him (1 Samuel 18:21).

questions.question: True or False: David's military success and wise behavior increased his popularity both with Saul's servants and the people of Israel.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: David’s wise behavior and success made him accepted and loved by Saul’s servants and all Israel (1 Samuel 18:5, 16).

questions.question: What was Saul's reaction to the women’s song comparing his military achievements to David's?
options: He was pleased and proud
He was angry and jealous
He ignored it
He rewarded David
questions.correctAnswer: He was angry and jealous
questions.explanation: Saul was very wroth because the women ascribed ten thousands to David and only thousands to him, fearing David's rise (1 Samuel 18:8).

questions.question: What cultural significance did the gift of Jonathan’s robe, sword, bow, and girdle to David hold?
options: It was a gift of friendship and symbolic transfer of honor
It was a sale of property
It was a sign of military surrender
It was a ritual of mourning
questions.correctAnswer: It was a gift of friendship and symbolic transfer of honor
questions.explanation: Jonathan stripping off his robe and giving his garments and weapons to David symbolized a deep bond and transfer of his princely honor to David (1 Samuel 18:4).

theological.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 18 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Samuel Chapter 18 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by Jonathan and David making a covenant because Jonathan loved David as his own soul?
options: The doctrine of sanctification through brotherly love
The doctrine of covenantal friendship reflecting God's covenant faithfulness
The doctrine of predestination
The doctrine of original sin
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of covenantal friendship reflecting God's covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:3 shows Jonathan and David making a covenant based on deep love, which illustrates how human covenants mirror God's faithful covenant relationships with His people (cf. Genesis 17:7).

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by the LORD's presence with David and departure from Saul as stated in this chapter?
options: Omnipotence
Faithfulness
Sovereignty and holiness
Immutability
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty and holiness
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:12 notes that the LORD was with David but had departed from Saul, revealing God's sovereign choice to withdraw favor due to Saul's disobedience, demonstrating His holiness and justice (cf. Psalm 7:11).

questions.question: How does David’s behavior and acceptance by the people and Saul’s servants (1 Samuel 18:5) contribute to understanding sanctification in the life of a believer?
options: Sanctification is a one-time event resulting in immediate perfection
Sanctification involves wise conduct and gaining favor through God's enabling
Sanctification is irrelevant to public acceptance
Sanctification is only about performing miracles
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves wise conduct and gaining favor through God's enabling
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:5 shows David behaving wisely and gaining acceptance, indicating sanctification as an ongoing process of godly behavior empowered by God (cf. Philippians 2:12-13).

questions.question: What does the jealousy of Saul in response to the women’s song (1 Samuel 18:7-8) reveal about human sinfulness and its consequences?
options: It reveals human humility
It reveals the sin of envy leading to spiritual downfall
It reveals the virtue of righteous anger
It reveals the necessity of political ambition
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals the sin of envy leading to spiritual downfall
questions.explanation: Saul's wrath and envy in 1 Samuel 18:8 demonstrate how envy and pride can lead to sin and estrangement from God, exemplifying the destructive nature of human sinfulness (cf. James 3:16).

questions.question: Considering 1 Samuel 18:27, what doctrine is illustrated by David’s military success and the bringing of Philistine foreskins as a dowry for Michal's hand in marriage?
options: The doctrine of justification by works
The doctrine of divine providence and human responsibility
The doctrine of monasticism
The doctrine of sacramental confession
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of divine providence and human responsibility
questions.explanation: David’s success in battle and fulfilling Saul’s demand (1 Samuel 18:27) illustrates how God providentially empowers believers while they actively engage in God-ordained responsibilities (cf. Proverbs 21:31).

questions.question: From 1 Samuel 18:10-11, what theological insight can be drawn about the presence of an 'evil spirit from God' affecting Saul?
options: God causes evil to tempt humans
God permits evil spirits as judgment or discipline over disobedient leaders
God is indifferent to spiritual warfare
Evil spirits have no role in the Old Testament
questions.correctAnswer: God permits evil spirits as judgment or discipline over disobedient leaders
questions.explanation: The passage in 1 Samuel 18:10-11 shows an evil spirit from God tormenting Saul, indicating God’s sovereign use of spiritual agents to discipline or bring judgment on sinful rulers (cf. Judges 9:23).

questions.question: What does the covenant and deep friendship between Jonathan and David (verses 1-4) typologically foreshadow in the New Testament?
options: The unity between Christ and the Church
The priesthood of believers
The relationship between Peter and Paul
The authority of kings over prophets
questions.correctAnswer: The unity between Christ and the Church
questions.explanation: Jonathan's covenant love for David (1 Samuel 18:1-4) typifies the profound and self-giving relationship Christ has with His Church (cf. Ephesians 5:25-27).

questions.question: How does David’s response to Saul’s offer of Merab’s daughter (1 Samuel 18:18) reflect an understanding of humility and God’s sovereign plan?
options: David arrogantly accepts the offer
David questions his worthiness, acknowledging God’s sovereign appointment
David rejects Saul outright
David demands compensation
questions.correctAnswer: David questions his worthiness, acknowledging God’s sovereign appointment
questions.explanation: David’s humble reply in 1 Samuel 18:18 reveals his awareness of his lowly status and God’s sovereign hand in his life, highlighting humility as a key biblical virtue (cf. James 4:6).

questions.question: What combined theological insight is gained by comparing 1 Samuel 18:14 and 1 Samuel 18:30 regarding David’s behavior and divine favor?
options: David’s wisdom is natural and unrelated to God
Divine favor accompanies wise and faithful leadership for God’s purposes
David’s success is due to political manipulation
God’s favor is unpredictable and random
questions.correctAnswer: Divine favor accompanies wise and faithful leadership for God’s purposes
questions.explanation: Verses 14 and 30 together show that David’s wise conduct and God’s presence with him result in honor and success, teaching that God blesses faithful leadership aligned with His will (cf. Proverbs 3:5-6).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that divine inspiration cannot coexist with the presence of an 'evil spirit from God' tormenting Saul. What does 1 Samuel 18:10-11 actually teach regarding God's sovereignty over spiritual forces?
options: God has no control over evil spirits
God sovereignly permits and uses spiritual agents—even evil ones—for His purposes, including judgment
Evil spirits act independently of God’s will
The passage is purely symbolic and not literal
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly permits and uses spiritual agents—even evil ones—for His purposes, including judgment
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 18:10-11 teaches that God’s sovereignty extends even over evil spirits, whom He can use to bring about discipline or judgment, affirming divine control over all creation (cf. Job 1:12).

questions.question: What doctrinal truth is demonstrated by Saul’s continual fear and enmity against David despite David’s loyalty (1 Samuel 18:29)?
options: The doctrine of perseverance of the saints
The doctrine of spiritual warfare and human depravity
The doctrine of universal reconciliation
The doctrine of election by works
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of spiritual warfare and human depravity
questions.explanation: Saul’s persistent hostility toward David (1 Samuel 18:29) reflects ongoing spiritual conflict rooted in human sinfulness and the reality of spiritual warfare (cf. Ephesians 6:12).

questions.question: How does Saul’s use of Michal’s love for David (1 Samuel 18:20-21) reveal human sinfulness and manipulation in the governance of Israel?
options: It reveals innocent affection without consequence
It reveals the sinful use of relationships for political and destructive ends
It reveals proper honoring of marriage
It shows divine approval of political marriages
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals the sinful use of relationships for political and destructive ends
questions.explanation: Saul’s intention to use Michal’s love as a snare (1 Samuel 18:21) shows sinful manipulation and misuse of personal relationships for political gain and destruction (cf. Proverbs 6:16-19).

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illuminated by David’s repeated wise conduct and God’s favor (1 Samuel 18:14, 15, 30) despite Saul’s increasing hostility?
options: The doctrine of divine providence and perseverance
The doctrine of predestination to damnation
The doctrine of faith without works
The doctrine of salvation by law
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of divine providence and perseverance
questions.explanation: David’s wise behavior and God's presence (18:14,15,30) alongside Saul’s hostility teach the doctrine that God providentially sustains His servants and enables them to persevere amid opposition (cf. Romans 8:28-39).

questions.question: What combined teaching about God’s justice and human pride is revealed by comparing Saul’s jealousy (1 Samuel 18:8) and David’s humility (1 Samuel 18:18)?
options: God favors the proud and punishes the humble
Human pride leads to downfall, while humility aligns with God’s righteous plan
Both Saul and David act with equal pride
Pride is indifferent to God’s justice
questions.correctAnswer: Human pride leads to downfall, while humility aligns with God’s righteous plan
questions.explanation: Saul’s jealous pride (18:8) contrasts with David’s humble questioning (18:18), teaching that pride incurs God’s judgment, while humility is honored in God’s justice (cf. Proverbs 16:18, James 4:10).

questions.question: How does the narrative of 1 Samuel 18 illustrate the biblical theme of God’s sovereignty in elevating a humble shepherd to kingship despite human opposition?
options: It shows that human effort alone determines leadership
It demonstrates God’s sovereign election of David over Saul despite Saul’s efforts to resist
It advocates for monarchy as a flawed institution
It denies any divine involvement in leadership
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates God’s sovereign election of David over Saul despite Saul’s efforts to resist
questions.explanation: The chapter shows that despite Saul’s hostility, God’s favor rests on David (18:12,29), fulfilling the theme of divine sovereignty in elevating His chosen king (cf. Psalm 78:70-72).
